# Takallum Kids (تَكَلُّم)

> Takallum Kids is a free web app that helps children aged about 4 to 11 speak Modern Standard Arabic (fusha). Each unit teaches a handful of words with a picture and audio, then the child says short sentences of two to four words built only from words already learned. No sign-up; progress is saved in the browser.

URL: https://takallum-kids.ummahapps.ai/
Publisher: Ummah Apps (https://ummahapps.ai/)
Price: free, no adverts
Age: about 4 to 11; made for children who can read Arabic letters with vowel marks, using it on their own
Interface language: English. Practice language: Modern Standard Arabic, fully vowelled.
Sister app for older learners: Takallum (https://takallum.ummahapps.ai/)

## How it works

1. **Meet the words**: each word card shows a picture, the vowelled Arabic and the English, and plays the audio.
2. **Say the words**: the child sees the picture, says the Arabic out loud, taps "Show me" to see and hear it, then taps "I said it!" or "Try again". Try-again words come back a little later in the same round.
3. **Say the sentences**: opens once every word in the unit is learned. Sentences use only words from that unit or earlier ones.
4. **Build the sentences**: the child taps the words of each sentence in the right order.
5. **Practise again**: a mix of up to 8 known words and sentences, weakest and least recently seen first.

Children who can't read Arabic yet can use Echo mode: each word and sentence is spoken first and the child says it back.

Each unit opens once the words in the one before are learned. Several children can share one device: each adds themselves with a name, an animal and "I'm a boy" or "I'm a girl", and keeps their own progress (tap the name at the top to switch). The boy/girl choice means sentences about themselves and the praise (أَحْسَنْتَ / أَحْسَنْتِ) match the child.

## Units (97 words, 104 sentences)

1. My family (عَائِلَتِي): هَذَا، هَذِهِ، أُمِّي، أَبِي، أَخِي، أُخْتِي. Sentences like هَذِهِ أُمِّي (This is my mum).
2. Hello (التَّحِيَّةُ): السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ، وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ، أَنَا، وَلَدٌ، بِنْتٌ، يَا، شُكْرًا. Sentences like شُكْرًا يَا أَبِي (Thank you, Dad).
3. Food (الطَّعَامُ): أُحِبُّ، أُرِيدُ، تُفَّاحَةٌ، مَوْزَةٌ، خُبْزٌ، حَلِيبٌ، مَاءٌ، جَائِعٌ. Sentences like أُرِيدُ مَاءً (I want water) and أَنَا جَائِعٌ / أَنَا جَائِعَةٌ (I am hungry).
4. Animals (الْحَيَوَانَاتُ): قِطٌّ، كَلْبٌ، فِيلٌ، سَمَكَةٌ، طَائِرٌ، كَبِيرٌ، صَغِيرٌ. Sentences like هَذِهِ سَمَكَةٌ صَغِيرَةٌ (This is a small fish).
5. Colours (الْأَلْوَانُ): أَحْمَرُ، أَصْفَرُ، أَخْضَرُ، أَزْرَقُ، أَبْيَضُ، أَسْوَدُ, with their feminine forms. Sentences like الْمَوْزَةُ صَفْرَاءُ (The banana is yellow).
6. At home (الْبَيْتُ): بَيْتٌ، أَيْنَ، فِي، هُنَا، كُرَةٌ، كِتَابٌ، سَرِيرٌ. Sentences like أَيْنَ الْكُرَةُ؟ (Where is the ball?).
7. Every day (كُلَّ يَوْمٍ): آكُلُ، أَشْرَبُ، أَلْعَبُ، أَنَامُ، أَقْرَأُ، مَعَ. Sentences like أَلْعَبُ مَعَ أَخِي (I play with my brother).
8. Yes, no and who (نَعَمْ وَلَا): نَعَمْ، لَا، هُوَ، هِيَ، مَا، مَنْ. Sentences like مَا هَذَا؟ (What is this?).
9. People I love (أَحْبَابِي): جَدِّي، جَدَّتِي، صَدِيقٌ، رَضِيعٌ، مُدَرِّسَةٌ. Sentences like أُحِبُّ جَدَّتِي (I love my grandma).
10. My body (جِسْمِي): رَأْسٌ، عَيْنٌ، أُذُنٌ، أَنْفٌ، فَمٌ، يَدٌ، رِجْلٌ. Sentences like هَذِهِ يَدِي (This is my hand).
11. School and things (الْمَدْرَسَةُ): مَدْرَسَةٌ، قَلَمٌ، حَقِيبَةٌ، كُرْسِيٌّ، سَيَّارَةٌ، عَلَى، تَحْتَ، إِلَى، أَذْهَبُ. Sentences like أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ (I go to school).
12. Yummy food (طَعَامٌ لَذِيذٌ): عَصِيرٌ، أَرُزٌّ، بَيْضٌ، دَجَاجٌ، كَعْكَةٌ، عِنَبٌ، لَذِيذٌ. Sentences like الْكَعْكَةُ لَذِيذَةٌ (The cake is delicious).
13. Outside (فِي الْحَدِيقَةِ): شَمْسٌ، قَمَرٌ، نَجْمٌ، شَجَرَةٌ، زَهْرَةٌ، حَدِيقَةٌ، جَمِيلٌ. Sentences like أَلْعَبُ فِي الْحَدِيقَةِ (I play in the garden).
14. More animals (حَيَوَانَاتٌ أُخْرَى): أَسَدٌ، حِصَانٌ، أَرْنَبٌ، بَقَرَةٌ. Sentences like أُرِيدُ أَرْنَبًا (I want a rabbit).
15. How I feel (مَشَاعِرِي): سَعِيدٌ، حَزِينٌ، خَائِفٌ، مُتْعَبٌ، عَطْشَانُ, each with a girl's form. Sentences like أَنَا سَعِيدٌ / أَنَا سَعِيدَةٌ (I am happy).

Units 8 to 15 add 50 words children use most from Kalimat (https://kalimat.ummahapps.ai/). Use Kalimat to practise words with games and Takallum Kids to make them into sentences.

## Features

- A picture (emoji) for every word and sentence
- Normal and slow audio using the device's Arabic text-to-speech voice, with step-by-step help for adding one
- Short tips for older children, e.g. why هَذِهِ goes with words ending in ة
- Works on phones and desktops; light and dark themes; the phone's back button steps back out of a round
